996.metaTitle: 996 hours — 9am to 9pm, six days a week
996.metaDescription: Open the browser countdown with 09:00–21:00 filled in. Twelve hours a day, seventy-two a week. Rotating or multi-shift calendars are on iOS.
996.intro: Nine in the morning to nine at night, six days a week — prefilled so the web timer can start from those two times.
body: 996 is shorthand for a day that runs from 9am to 9pm, six days a week. It began as a description of working hours at parts of China's technology industry, and the number is now used well beyond that context.
The arithmetic is what makes it notable. Twelve clock hours a day across six days is seventy-two hours a week — close to double a conventional forty-hour week, and that is before any commuting.

In August 2021 China's Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security jointly published a set of labour dispute cases stating that 996 arrangements exceed the statutory limits on working hours. Whether that applies to any particular job is a question for your own contract and local rules.

The web timer measures the interval you set, from start to finish, including days this long. It does not keep a weekly roster or switch you between several patterns. If 09:00–21:00 is today's stretch, start the countdown; if your day is different, change either time on the home page.
Use the browser when you want one start, one end, and nothing to install. Use iOS when the week itself changes — alternating weeks, work/rest rotations, or more than one kind of day.

9-to-5.name: 9 to 5
9-to-5.metaTitle: How many hours is 9 to 5? 8 hours, 40 a week
9-to-5.metaDescription: 9 to 5 is 8 hours a day and 40 a week. With an unpaid 30- or 60-minute lunch it is 7.5 or 7 paid hours. Start a countdown with these times in your browser.
9-to-5.intro: 9 to 5 is 8 hours: 09:00 to 17:00, five days a week, 40 hours in total. If lunch is unpaid, it is 7.5 hours with a 30-minute break and 7 hours with a 60-minute break.
body: Nine to five is the shorthand for a standard working day: eight hours at work, five days a week, forty hours in total. In the United States the forty-hour week was written into law by the Fair Labor Standards Act in 1938, and the phrase has since become the general name for regular office hours in English.

Strictly speaking, nine to five is eight hours only where the lunch break is paid. Where it is unpaid, the same clock hours usually amount to seven or seven and a half hours of paid time — worth checking before you compare two offers by their hours alone.

The web countdown measures the clock hours you set, from start to finish. If you want it to reflect paid time only, set the end time an hour earlier on the home page. It will not build a week of mixed days; that belongs in the iOS app.
Stay in the browser for a single 09:00–17:00 stretch. Reach for iOS when you need several shift kinds or a roster that repeats on its own.

9-to-6.name: 9 to 6
9-to-6.metaTitle: How many hours is 9 to 6? 9 hours, 45 a week
9-to-6.metaDescription: 9 to 6 is 9 hours a day and 45 a week. With an unpaid 60-minute lunch it is 8 paid hours, the same as 9 to 5. Start a countdown with these times in your browser.
9-to-6.intro: 9 to 6 is 9 hours: 09:00 to 18:00, five days a week, 45 hours in total. With an unpaid one-hour lunch it comes to 8 paid hours a day.
body: Nine to six is the common office day across much of East and Southeast Asia: nine clock hours from start to finish, five days a week, forty-five in total.
The extra hour compared with nine to five is usually the unpaid lunch break, which is why the two patterns often amount to the same quantity of paid work despite the different-looking numbers.

Start the web countdown to track the nine hours from start to finish, or adjust the end time on the home page if your break is counted differently. The page only prefills two times; it does not rotate you through a set of days.
Keep the browser timer for one 09:00–18:00 interval. Use iOS when the week mixes patterns or follows a work/rest cycle.

night-shift.name: Night shift
night-shift.metaTitle: Night hours — a countdown that crosses midnight
night-shift.metaDescription: Open the browser countdown with 22:00–06:00 filled in. End earlier than start is treated as overnight. Multi-shift rosters are on iOS.
night-shift.intro: Ten at night to six the following morning — prefilled so the web timer can follow a day that crosses midnight.
body: A night stretch is the case where a naive countdown breaks: the finishing time is earlier on the clock than the starting time, so subtracting one from the other gives a negative number.

The web timer reads an end that is earlier than its start as one that crosses midnight. Opening it at one in the morning shows five hours left of the stretch that began the previous evening, rather than twenty-nine hours until tonight's.

The same handling applies to any overnight pair, not just ten to six — set your own hours on the home page and the interval is anchored the same way. What the browser will not do is keep several overnight patterns in a rotating calendar.
Use this page when today's only question is 22:00–06:00. Use iOS when nights, days and rest days have to take turns.
